Launch an Interactive Shiny App to Explore a Network Graph

Source: R/launch_network_app.R
launch_network_app.Rd

Interpreting clusters means going back and forth between the structure of the network and its content: which documents form this cluster, who wrote them, when, which ones sit at its border? launch_network_app() opens a local Shiny application for this reading. The network is drawn with interactive nodes (with tooltips) and cluster labels; clicking a cluster displays the metadata of its nodes (cluster_information) in a searchable table. Node size, edge width, labels and the visibility of edges can be adjusted to make dense networks readable. For a list of networks (one per time window), a menu selects the window.

If layout is given, coordinates are computed with layout_networks(), replacing any existing x and y; with layout = NULL, the existing x and y columns are used. The app needs the shiny, ggiraph, DT and shinycssloaders packages.

Usage

launch_network_app(
  graph_tbl,
  cluster_id,
  cluster_information,
  cluster_tooltip = NULL,
  node_id,
  node_tooltip = NULL,
  node_size = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  layout = "fr"
)

Arguments

graph_tbl

A tbl_graph object with or without layout coordinates.

cluster_id

Column name in the node data identifying clusters. It can be the cluster ID or a unique label for each cluster.

cluster_information

Character vector of node metadata columns to display in the data table.

cluster_tooltip

Optional. Fixed text string to display when hovering over cluster labels (not a column name).

node_id

Column name identifying node IDs.

node_tooltip

Optional. Column name for tooltips shown when hovering over nodes.

node_size

Optional. Column name used to scale node size.

color

Optional. Column name used to color nodes. If NULL, colors are automatically assigned using networkflow::color_networks(column_to_color = cluster_id).

layout

Character. Name of a layout to compute node coordinates (e.g. "fr", "kk"). If specified, this replaces any existing layout. If NULL, existing x/y coordinates are used.

Value

A Shiny app interface for exploring the network.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
network <- build_network(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  projection_method = "structured",
  cooccurrence_method = "coupling_angle",
  edges_threshold = 1
)
network <- add_clusters(network, clustering_method = "leiden",
                        objective_function = "modularity", seed = 123)

launch_network_app(
  graph_tbl = network,
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  cluster_information = c("source_author", "source_title", "source_year", "source_journal"),
  node_id = "source_id",
  node_tooltip = "source_label",
  layout = "fr"
)

# One network per time window: the app shows a menu of windows
networks <- build_dynamic_networks(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  time_variable = "source_year",
  time_window = 20,
  window_step = 1,
  cooccurrence_method = "coupling_angle"
)
networks <- add_clusters(networks, clustering_method = "leiden",
                         objective_function = "modularity", seed = 123)
launch_network_app(
  graph_tbl = networks,
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  cluster_information = c("source_author", "source_title", "source_year"),
  node_id = "source_id",
  layout = "fr"
)
} # }
